audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers gave opposite answers to every row: full-layer sides read Fizz 7/7, content win[] read Brand 7/7. The packet flags the content chart directly — 'Brand wins only 42.3% but the chart gives Brand 7/7 stages vs 0' across 487 games.
audit.why: Both charts are partly right. Brand's Q reaches 1050 against a 550-range Urchin Strike and a 400-range Playful, so levels 1-3 genuinely belong to Brand. Seastone Trident falls to a 4-second cooldown by rank 4, which evens levels 4-5, and from level 6 a 1300-range Chum the Waters plus an untargetable hop takes the matchup for good. That shape is what a 42.3% win rate looks like.
audit.corrected: Brand, Brand, Brand, Skill, Fizz, Fizz, Fizz — proposed as one group with the matching content win[] rows and every why rewritten to argue its own verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4]-whys[6], mid and late all claimed Brand pre-empts the level 6 all-in and that his engage window 'keeps shrinking' with items.
audit.why: The opposite is true after one item: Chum the Waters attaches from 1300 range and knocks you up for the full Urchin Strike follow-up, and Playful / Trickster is untargetable, so the spell you spend to answer him is erased. Brand has no dash and no escape.
audit.corrected: Level 6 onward rewritten as Fizz's phase, with Brand's answer stated as Zhonya's, peel and positioning rather than a duel.

audit.whatIsWrong: Seastone Trident's auto-attack reset was never mentioned, and the page treated Sear as a reliable answer to the hop.
audit.why: Fizz's combo opens with an empowered attack, so the auto wind-up rather than an ability cast is the cue to step back. And Sear is a projectile that must hit a champion — thrown at Playful it hits an untargetable model and is wasted. Hold it for the landing.
audit.corrected: Stated in dontsFull[2].d, breakdown.cooldowns and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit; dosFull[2].d called Playful / Trickster a 'fifteen-second' cooldown.
audit.why: It is 16/14/12/10/8 — sixteen at rank 1, eight at rank 5. Chum the Waters is 120s at rank 1, Urchin Strike 8s.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into both fields.

edits.before: From level 3 onward Brand strings Q into E for a full ablaze detonation the instant Fizz enters W's AoE, meaning any minion-wave push Fizz attempts gets answered with burst that outpaces his crab poke. At 6, Fizz's Chum the Waters finally gives him a real all-in, but the shark telegraphs long enough for Brand to walk out of it or drop W on the water's landing spot to threaten the follow-up combo before Fizz can capitalize. Because Brand's rotation punishes the approach rather than the finish, Fizz is stuck choosing between an all-in that gets pre-empted and passive farming that concedes priority — neither lets him flip the lane.
edits.after: From level 3 your Q into E detonates a real chunk the moment Fizz steps in, and W alone zones the wave, so through level 5 he farms on your terms. Level 6 is the hinge: Chum the Waters throws from 1300 range, attaches to you, and the shark knocks you up long enough for the whole Urchin Strike follow-up. Playful / Trickster is 16 seconds at rank 1 and turns him untargetable mid-hop, which means a Sear thrown at the jump is a wasted stun. Hold Q for the landing rather than the takeoff, keep the wave shoved so a dive costs him a long walk, and stop stepping past your minions once his ultimate is up.

edits.before: With a Luden's or equivalent burst item, Brand's poke alone approaches kill-threshold on squishies, so Fizz can no longer walk up for a slow trade without risking death from full HP. His only out is a double-jump all-in, but Zhonya's or Stopwatch timing gets eaten by burn ticking through the invuln window, and Sear's stun range now extends far enough that E-flash engages get intercepted before he's even airborne. In teamfights Brand's W zones the exact chokepoints Fizz needs to flank through, so his engage window keeps shrinking as items scale — he's forced to either eat a stun approaching or concede the fight entirely.
edits.after: Past one item this flips. Chum the Waters throws from 1300 range, sticks to you, and knocks you up for a full combo, while Playful / Trickster turns him untargetable at will — the one spell you spend to answer him is erased, and Sear has to land on a champion who is airborne. Your answer is not a duel. Buy Zhonya's, stand behind your frontline, and treat the shark as the cast you save every defensive cooldown for. In teamfights your value is unchanged — spread Blaze with E and let Pyroclasm bounce through the clump — but expect to be his opening target, so position on the far side of your team and never be the closest body to a warded wall.
